items.q: Can foreigners really buy property in Saudi Arabia now?
items.a: Yes. REGA announced that the Law of Real Estate Ownership by Non-Saudis came into force on 22 January 2026. It covers Riyadh, Jeddah, Makkah and Madinah, inside zones designated by the government. The Executive Regulations and the zones were approved on 23 June 2026. In Makkah and Madinah, ownership is limited to Muslim individuals and Saudi companies. Always check the exact property on REGA's official zone map.

On REGA's Saudi Properties portal (saudiproperties.rega.gov.sa). Residents apply with their Iqama number. People living abroad first get a Saudi digital identity through a Saudi embassy, and also need a Saudi bank account and mobile number in their own name. Foreign companies first register with the Ministry of Investment.

items.q: Does buying a home give me residency?
items.a: No, not by itself. Residency comes from your work visa (Iqama) or from Premium Residency. The Real Estate Owner Premium Residency is a separate application for owners of residential property worth at least SAR 4 million that is not mortgaged. Check current conditions on sapr.gov.sa.

items.q: What will I pay on top of the price?
items.a: 5% Real Estate Transaction Tax, brokerage (2.5% unless agreed otherwise) plus 15% VAT on the commission, and financing costs if you take a mortgage. When a non-Saudi later sells in Riyadh, Jeddah, Makkah or Madinah, REGA charges a 2% fee.

items.q: Are the prices on Miftah AI real?
items.a: Not yet. Until the official Ministry of Justice data feed is connected, district prices, deal counts and trends are sample data and are labelled as such on every page and report. Do not use them to judge a real price.

items.q: Is Miftah AI part of the government, a broker or a lawyer?
items.a: None of these. Miftah AI is an independent company. We explain the official rules and link to them so you can check for yourself. We do not sell property, recommend what to buy, or give legal or financial advice.
English, Arabic, Urdu, Hindi and Chinese. The advisor replies in the language you write in.

When Saudi Arabia opened property ownership to non-Saudis in 2026, millions of people, residents and investors alike, suddenly had a new door in front of them. But the key was missing: clear answers in their language, from official data. We're building that key.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Miftah AI respects your privacy and is designed to comply with the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL). We collect the minimum data needed to run the service.

sections.p: Account and contact details you give us (email, name, nationality, city of interest, role, preferred language), questions you ask the advisor, and basic anonymous usage analytics.
To provide and improve the service, answer your messages, send updates you've agreed to, and check the quality and accuracy of AI answers.
Only as long as needed for these purposes. Chat logs are reviewed for quality and deleted or anonymised on a regular schedule.
Only service providers that help us run Miftah AI (such as hosting, database, email and analytics), under contracts that protect your data. We never sell personal data.
You can ask to access, correct or delete your data, or withdraw consent, at any time through the contact page on this website.
Questions about privacy: through the contact page on this website.

terms.intro: By using Miftah AI you agree to these terms. Please read them together with our Disclaimer and Privacy Policy.

sections.p: Miftah AI provides information about Saudi property based on official open data and published regulations. It does not list properties for sale or act as a broker.
Nothing on Miftah AI is legal, financial, tax or brokerage advice. You are responsible for your own decisions and should consult licensed professionals.
We work hard to keep data accurate and sourced, but official data can be delayed or incomplete and rules can change. Always verify with official sources.
Do not misuse the service, attempt to scrape it, resell its data without a licence, or use it for unlawful purposes.

Miftah AI Pro is a monthly subscription. Our order process is conducted by our online reseller Paddle.com. Paddle.com is the Merchant of Record for all our orders and handles payment, VAT, billing enquiries and refunds; Paddle's buyer terms also apply to your purchase.

Subscriptions renew automatically each month until cancelled. You can cancel at any time from Plan & billing → Manage billing; you keep Pro until the end of the period already paid for. Refunds follow our Refund Policy.
We may update these terms. Continued use means you accept the updated terms.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.intro: Miftah AI is an information service. Please read this carefully.

sections.p: Miftah AI is not a lawyer, licensed real estate broker, tax adviser or financial adviser. We give facts so you can decide; we do not tell you what to buy.
Prices are based on registered transactions from official sources, usually updated quarterly. They are recorded deal prices, not live asking prices, and are shown at district level.
Zone status is based on official publications and is re-checked regularly. Where status is 'to be verified', you must confirm with REGA or a licensed broker before buying.
Some district price figures are illustrative samples until the official Ministry of Justice price feed is connected. They are clearly labelled as samples. Do not use them for decisions.
Data from the Ministry of Justice, REGA, KAPSARC and OpenStreetMap belongs to its owners and is used under their open-data terms with attribution.

refunds.title: Refund Policy
refunds.intro: We want you to be confident subscribing to Miftah AI Pro. This policy explains when you can get your money back. Payments are processed by Paddle.com, our merchant of record.

sections.p: If Miftah AI Pro is not right for you, ask for a refund within 14 days of your first subscription payment and we will refund it in full, no questions asked.
Monthly renewals are not refunded once the new month has started, but you can cancel at any time to stop future charges. You keep Pro until the end of the period you have paid for.
If you were charged twice, charged after cancelling, or charged in error, we refund the incorrect amount in full.

Reply to your Paddle receipt email, use paddle.net to find your order, or contact us from the Contact page with the email address you paid with. Refunds go back to the original payment method, usually within 5 to 10 business days.
This policy does not limit any rights you have under the consumer law that applies to you.

guide.title: Buying and settling in Saudi Arabia as a foreigner
guide.subtitle: A plain, step-by-step guide to the 2026 rules: who can buy, where, how to apply, the full cost, and what owning a home means for residency.
guide.caution: This guide is a plain-language summary of official rules, written by Miftah AI. It is not legal advice. Rules can change, so confirm every point with the official source before you act.

sections.title: Can a foreigner buy property?
sections.intro: Yes. REGA announced that the Law of Real Estate Ownership by Non-Saudis came into force on 22 January 2026.
points: Who can buy: non-Saudi individuals living in the Kingdom or abroad, foreign companies, foreign non-profit entities, and Saudi companies with foreign shareholders.

Where: the law covers Riyadh, Jeddah, Makkah and Madinah, inside zones designated by the government. The Council of Ministers approved the zones and the Executive Regulations on 23 June 2026. REGA shows them on its official zone map.
Makkah and Madinah: ownership is limited to Muslim individuals and Saudi companies.
Outside the designated zones, ownership is more limited and depends on who you are. Do not assume a district is open until you have checked the official map.
sections.note: Older articles that describe the 2000 law (ownership only with a Ministry of Interior permit) are out of date.

sections.title: How to apply
points: Everything is done online on REGA's Saudi Properties portal (saudiproperties.rega.gov.sa).
If you live in Saudi Arabia: apply with your Iqama number. Eligibility is checked automatically.
If you live abroad: first get a Saudi digital identity through a Saudi embassy or consulate. You also need a bank account in Saudi Arabia and a Saudi mobile number, both in your own name.
If you are a foreign company: register with the Ministry of Investment (Invest Saudi) to get a Unified Number starting with 700, then apply.
sections.note: Use only the official portal. Be careful with anyone who offers to 'register' your ownership for a fee.

sections.title: Buying, step by step
points: Find the exact property on REGA's official zone map and confirm it is open to you.
Use a FAL-licensed broker only. Every property advert must show a REGA advertising licence number.
Check the title deed: it must be electronic, in the seller's name, and free of mortgages or disputes. Deeds can be checked through Najiz.
Buying off-plan? Ask for the project's Wafi licence. Your payments must go into the project's escrow account.
Sign the contract, pay the 5% transaction tax through ZATCA, then complete the transfer of the deed electronically.
Pay only through regulated electronic channels. Never pay a deposit in cash or into a personal account.

sections.title: The full cost
sections.intro: On top of the price, plan for:
points: 5% Real Estate Transaction Tax on the value (ZATCA). By law the seller owes it, but the contract can say who pays.
Brokerage: 2.5% of the price unless you agree a different rate in writing, plus 15% VAT on the commission.
A 2% REGA fee when a non-Saudi later sells or disposes of property in Riyadh, Jeddah, Makkah or Madinah.
Bank valuation, financing and service costs if you take a mortgage.
sections.note: Example: on a SAR 1,000,000 flat bought through a broker, if you pay the tax, the extra cost is about SAR 78,750 (SAR 50,000 tax + SAR 25,000 commission + SAR 3,750 VAT). Use the cost calculator for your own numbers.

sections.title: Settling in Saudi Arabia: home and residency
sections.intro: Owning a home and the right to live in the Kingdom are two separate things.
points: Buying a property does not give you residency by itself. Most expats live here on a work residency (Iqama).

Premium Residency is a separate route. One product, Real Estate Owner residency, is for owners of residential property worth at least SAR 4 million that is not mortgaged. Its fee is reported as SAR 4,000. Check current conditions on sapr.gov.sa.
Premium Residency holders can live with their family, sponsor relatives and own property, except in Makkah, Madinah and border areas.
Renting: leases are registered on Ejar. In Riyadh, rent increases inside the city boundary were frozen for five years from September 2025.
Before you buy, think about what happens if your job or Iqama ends, and ask a licensed professional about your own situation.

mistakes: Paying a deposit before checking the zone map, the broker's FAL licence and the title deed.
Trusting a social media advert that shows no REGA licence number.
Paying someone to 'register' your ownership. Applications are made on the official portal.
Relying on old articles about the 2000 law, or on the 10% fee figure from 2025 news coverage.
Assuming that buying a flat gives you or your family residency.
Paying in cash or into a personal bank account.
guide.checksBody: You don't have to take our word for anything. These official services let you check each point yourself.
